description: Scatter this step's keys/values (or MLA latent + rope) into the paged KV pool at slot_mapping, optionally quantizing to the cache dtype. reshape_and_cache(_flash), set_mla_kv_buffer, concat_and_cache_mla, fused rope+cache writers.

has_value.doc: false for an MLA latent cache (one tensor)

hooks.slot_mapping: (name, spec, shape, dtype, sym, gen, device) -> (slots, logical): distinct slots in [0, pool_slots), scattered the way a long-running server's allocator leaves them (a shuffled pool, not arange), with -1 for padded tokens if the deployment pads.
hooks.cache_layout: (t, name, sym) -> the cache stored in the layout the kernel writes (paged [num_blocks, block_size, heads, dim], aiter's x-packed key layout, an MLA [slots, 1, 576] latent with packed scales...). Reshape/view only; the contents are zeros.

call: Clone k_cache/v_cache inside call(), invoke the writer on the clones and return them (k_cache_out, v_cache_out): the comparison is over the whole pool, so a write to a wrong slot shows up as well as a wrong value.

timing.cache: writes are scattered over a pool much larger than L2; read-evict is close to serving.

negative_controls: write slot s + 1: the whole pool differs at two rows per token
skip the fp8 scale on the value path: every written value byte differs
pitfalls: Comparing only the written rows misses an out-of-bounds or wrong-slot write; compare the entire pool, which starts identically zeroed in both legs.
A contiguous slot_mapping (arange) hides stride bugs that a scattered pool exposes and is cheaper to time than served.
For an fp8 cache the quantization is part of the op: bytes_exact holds because every correct writer computes the same scaled cast; a candidate changing the rounding mode is a different op.
